stem: An attacker gets a victim to log in with a session ID the attacker already knows, then reuses that ID. Which fix stops this?
options: Store the session ID in the URL
Issue a new session ID when the user authenticates
Disable HTTPS on the login page
explanation: Session fixation works when the pre-login session ID survives authentication.
optionNotes: IDs in URLs leak through logs and referrers.
Shorter IDs are easier to guess.

stem: To inject data into an existing TCP session without seeing its traffic, what must an attacker predict?
explanation: Randomized initial sequence numbers (RFC 6528) make blind injection very hard.
optionNotes: An application header, not a TCP value.
Irrelevant to accepting a TCP segment.

stem: Which cookie attribute stops page JavaScript from reading a session cookie?
explanation: Use HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite together on session cookies.
optionNotes: Secure sends the cookie over HTTPS only.
Domain sets which hosts receive the cookie.
Correct: this limits the damage of XSS cookie theft.
